product_backlog.description: Core to-do list management and UI capabilities
product_backlog.title: Core To-Do App MVP

acceptance_criteria: - Given the application is running, When the user views the home page, Then they see an option to create a new to-do list with a name.
- Given the user enters a list name, When they submit the form, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed in the lists view.
product_backlog.title: Create a new to-do list
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully initialize and view named to-do lists.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can add descriptive tasks to specific lists.
acceptance_criteria: - Given an existing to-do list, When the user adds a task with a short text description, Then the task appears within that list.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.
product_backlog.title: Add a task to a list
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.

acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user clicks to mark it complete/incomplete, Then its status toggles and is visually updated.
product_backlog.title: Mark a task as complete or incomplete
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can toggle task completion status with visual feedback.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.

product_backlog.title: Delete a task
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can remove individual tasks from lists.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove unwanted items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user clicks delete on the task, Then the task is removed from the list.

product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete projects or categories.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can delete lists and all contained tasks cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing list with tasks, When the user clicks delete on the entire list, Then the list and all its associated tasks are removed.
product_backlog.title: Delete an entire list and its tasks
View lists and tasks with visual distinction for completed items
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all my lists and their tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a clear overview of my work.
acceptance_criteria: Given multiple lists and tasks exist, When the user views the main application page, Then all lists and their tasks are displayed, with completed tasks visually distinguished (e.g., struck-through or grayed out) from incomplete ones.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users get a clear overview of all lists and tasks with visual distinction for completion.

sprint_backlog.approach: We will use Python with Flask and SQLite (via SQLAlchemy or raw sqlite3) to build a clean, lightweight, and robust To-Do List web application with a responsive HTML/CSS frontend. This ensures fast execution, easy local setup, and reliable persistence for single-user scenarios.
tasks: 1. Initialize Flask app structure with templates and static folders
2. Implement database schema for Lists and Tasks
3. Implement routes and UI for creating lists and adding tasks
sprint_backlog.test_approach: Unit tests for Flask routes and database models using pytest.
risks_assumptions: Assuming SQLite provides adequate file-based persistence for single-user sessions without heavy DB setup.

The product vision for this entire evaluation, verbatim, is:

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team
> produced.** Its entire value is being byte-identical across runs, so results are
> comparable across Horseless Carriage versions over time. If the scenario itself

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.


Treat the sprint goal and backlog for this sprint as pre-approved by me (the human) - do not wait for further approval messages, proceed directly through planning, development, PR creation, CI verification, sprint review (create_sprint_report), and the release PR (create_release_pr) for this sprint's increment. Do not ask me anything else during this sprint - make reasonable decisions yourself and note them as assumptions in the sprint report.
